analysis.title: Prime Insights & Analytics Chart Pack, November 2026
key_insights: Global Fundamental L/S funds are down -0.2% MTD in November (+8.9% YTD as of Nov 16), with beta losses partly offset by positive alpha from short-side gains. Systematic L/S is up +1.1% MTD and +17.4% YTD after a sharp recovery last week.

TMT L/S funds are down -4.5% MTD (+0.6% YTD) and Asia L/S funds are down -1.4% MTD (+12.6% YTD). Europe L/S is +0.3% MTD (+8% YTD), US L/S is -0.2% MTD (+6.3% YTD) and Health Care L/S is +0.2% MTD (+8.7% YTD).

Fundamental L/S alpha is +0.6% MTD (+7.2% YTD), driven by short-side gains. Asset Selection, Short Concentration and Size are the largest alpha contributors in November, partly offset by losses in Momentum factors and Volatility.

Hedge funds net sold global equities heavily in November, with long and short sales at about 3 to 1. Trailing 4-week de-grossing in global equities is the largest since Feb 2023 and one of the largest in the past decade.

Single stocks were net sold in 7 of the last 8 weeks, and selling has picked up in November. ETF short flows have become more volatile, which the desk reads as investors using macro products to hedge and manage exposure.
Fundamental L/S net leverage fell -7.6 pts MTD to 41.6%, a 5-year low and below the Liberation Day lows. Gross leverage fell -4.4 pts MTD to 206.3% (23rd percentile 1-year, 65th percentile 3-year).

The desk says equities could set up for a tactical rally in the near term after the de-grossing, as seasonality and technicals turn friendlier. GIR's Sentiment Indicator and Risk Appetite Indicator do not show capitulation by the broader set of market participants.
EM Asia and North America are heavily net sold in November, while Europe and DM Asia see modest net buying driven by short covers. Taiwan, Korea and China are the most net sold Asian markets MTD.
Hedge funds are overweight Asia (DM + EM) by +8.4% relative to MSCI World ACWI, compared with a record +20% in June and +6.5% at the start of 2026.

Selling of global Info Tech over the trailing 6 weeks is the fastest in the past decade (-4.4 z score), led by Semis & Semi Equip. The global Info Tech long/short ratio is 1.79 against a YTD peak of 2.9, approaching 10-year lows.
Info Tech is the most net sold US sector in November, led by heavy shorting in Semis & Semi Equip. US Semis net exposure is below US Software net exposure for the first time since the start of 2026.

Industrials is the second most net sold US sector MTD, with short and long sales at about 2 to 1. Nearly all subsectors are net sold, led by Electrical Equip, Ground Transportation and Construction & Engineering. Net exposure is at its lowest in more than two years.

Consumer Staples is among the most net sold US sectors MTD, which the desk reads as hedge funds fading the sector's price rally. Staples Retail & Distribution, Personal Care Products and Beverages lead the selling.
Hedge funds have unwound US Health Care risk for 9 consecutive weeks, led by Biotech de-grossing since mid-August. Biotech de-grossing accelerated in November, driven by long sales.

Exposure to Medium-Term Momentum is on track to fall for a 6th straight month to its lowest level since Dec 2022 (20th percentile 5-year). Exposure to Value has risen sharply to 5-year highs amid increased stagflation concerns.
